title: 1.11.2 - IPv6 Cluster creation stuck trying to get quorum status from first MON
body: I am creating an IPv6-only Kubernetes cluster with rook/ceph:v1.11.2-4.g9928f26cc and Ceph v17.2.5. My CephCluster sets ipFamily: "IPv6", dualStack: false, requireMsgr2: true, and requests three MONs. The first MON starts, but the operator cannot get quorum status, so no further MONs are created and cluster creation does not proceed. I expect all MONs to be created and reach quorum.

symptoms_visible: With IPv6 only and requireMsgr2 set to true, the first MON comes up, but no additional MONs are created and the cluster never reaches quorum.
N0.label: N0 IPv6 msgr2 bootstrap stalled

symptoms_visible: The IPv6 cluster proceeds through creation when I set requireMsgr2 to false; with it true from the beginning, creation remains stuck after the first MON.
N1.label: N1 configuration probe isolates msgr2 bootstrap path

symptoms_visible: The first MON remains in probing state with an empty quorum.
Its status reports the v2 peer as '[fd07:aaaa:bbbb:cccc::11:3300]:3300', and rook-ceph.config contains 'mon host = [v2:fd07:aaaa:bbbb:cccc::11:3300]'.
The operator also logs that endpoints such as '[fd07:aaaa:bbbb:cccc::11]:6789' do not contain two parts from which to extract the port.
N2.label: N2 malformed IPv6 monitor endpoints observed

symptoms_visible: The generated requireMsgr2 configuration lacks brackets around the IPv6 host before the port.
The other generation path produces 'v2:[fd07:aaaa:bbbb:cccc::11]:3300', which has the IPv6 address bracketed separately from the port.
N3.label: N3 endpoint construction difference located

symptoms_visible: With my patched operator image, rook-ceph.config contains 'mon host = [v2:[fd07:aaaa:bbbb:cccc::11]:3300]'.
The cluster creates three MONs in quorum a,b,c, and the manager service has one active daemon and one standby.
N4.label: N4 patched operator verified on reporter cluster

symptoms_visible: An IPv6-only cluster using the corrected operator starts all three MONs with msgr2 required, reaches quorum, and brings the manager daemons online.
N_terminal.label: terminal IPv6 msgr2 bootstrap resolved

question_patterns: Can you temporarily set requireMsgr2 to false and report whether cluster creation proceeds?
Does the same IPv6-only cluster bootstrap if you repeat the test without requiring msgr2?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. With requireMsgr2 set to false, cluster creation proceeds. With it true from the initial creation, it hangs after the first MON.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It remains stuck after the first MON with requireMsgr2 false as well.
It also proceeds with requireMsgr2 false, but takes a little longer before creating the second MON.

edges.comment: Thread c2-c5, reporter's cluster: participant2 requested the configuration-toggle probe. The reporter observed successful bootstrap with the setting disabled and separately volunteered that another bare-metal IPv6 Ceph cluster works with msgr2 enabled after bootstrap. This is a measurement, not the final fix.

question_patterns: What errors does the operator log while it is processing the monitor endpoints?
Can you paste the relevant operator log lines from the stalled cluster?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The operator repeatedly prints errors like: endpoint "[fd07:aaaa:bbbb:cccc::11]:6789" does not contain two parts to extract the port. It prints the same error for the other monitor addresses.

question_patterns: Can you connect to the first MON's admin socket and share its mon_status output?
What address does the first MON report while it is stuck probing?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The first MON is rank -1 and state probing with no quorum. Its extra probe peer is shown as "[fd07:aaaa:bbbb:cccc::11:3300]:3300", and its monmap has no recognized public address.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The MON reports the peer as "[fd07:aaaa:bbbb:cccc::11]:3300", with a recognized public address, but it still cannot form quorum.

question_patterns: What is the exact mon host line in the generated rook-ceph.config for the failed bootstrap?
Can you inspect the generated Ceph configuration and paste the monitor endpoint?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The generated file says: mon host = [v2:fd07:aaaa:bbbb:cccc::11:3300].

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The generated file says: mon host = [v2:[fd07:aaaa:bbbb:cccc::11]:3300], so the IPv6 address and port are already separated by brackets.

edges.comment: Thread c6 and c15-c16, reporter's cluster: the reporter supplied raw operator errors, first-MON admin-socket output, and the generated configuration. The conclusion that these values come from incorrect host/port construction is not placed in the reporter's answers.

question_patterns: Can you trace where this monitor endpoint is generated and compare it with the path that produces a working endpoint?
Which source location constructs the malformed mon host value, and how does the adjacent working path differ?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I traced it to the require-msgr2 branch in pkg/daemon/ceph/client/config.go. That branch builds the value by directly combining the monitor IP and 3300. The following path uses net.JoinHostPort. I think using JoinHostPort in the first branch would handle the IPv6 brackets correctly.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Both branches already use net.JoinHostPort and produce identical bracketed output, so I could not find a source-level formatting difference.

question_patterns: What exact monitor endpoint does the working generation path produce?
Can you paste the generated mon host line from the configuration that formats the IPv6 endpoints successfully?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The working path produces: mon host = [v2:[fd07:aaaa:bbbb:cccc::11]:3300,v1:[fd07:aaaa:bbbb:cccc::11]:6789]. That shows the IPv6 host bracketed before each port.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The working path uses a different IPv6 address but has the same v2:[address]:3300 and v1:[address]:6789 structure.

edges.comment: Thread c17-c18 and c25-c26, reporter's investigation: the reporter located the construction branch, proposed net.JoinHostPort, opened a patch, and showed the correctly formatted output from the adjacent path. These are source and output observations produced by the reporter.

question_patterns: Can you build and deploy an operator image from your branch, then paste the generated mon host line?
Please test your patched operator on the IPv6 cluster and report the exact generated endpoint.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I built and pushed an operator image from my branch. With requireMsgr2 true, the generated line is now: mon host = [v2:[fd07:aaaa:bbbb:cccc::11]:3300].

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The patched operator still generates mon host = [v2:fd07:aaaa:bbbb:cccc::11:3300].

question_patterns: After deploying the test image, does the cluster finish creating its MONs, and what does ceph status report?
Please report the quorum and manager status from the cluster running the test build.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I have three MONs now, all in quorum, and the rest of the cluster is coming online. ceph status shows mon: 3 daemons, quorum a,b,c; mgr: b active with a standby. I have no OSDs yet because I still need to reclaim the drives, so the only warning is that the OSD count is zero. As far as the MON and MGR situation is concerned, it looks correct. I think that solved the issue.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The endpoint is formatted correctly, but the test cluster still creates only one MON and never reaches quorum.
The three MONs reach quorum, but ceph status warns that there are no OSDs because I have not made the drives available yet.

edges.comment: Thread c19-c30, reporter's own cluster: after receiving build and image-publishing instructions, the reporter deployed the branch image, showed the corrected raw configuration, and confirmed three-MON quorum plus active/standby MGRs. This is pre-landing candidate-build verification and remains a measurement clarification.

solution.intent: Correct the IPv6 monitor endpoint construction used when msgr2 is required so that the IPv6 literal is bracketed before the port is appended, then ship the validated operator change.
solution.concrete_example: Generate the v2 monitor endpoint with net.JoinHostPort instead of directly concatenating the IPv6 address and port. The resulting Ceph entry must have the form [v2:[fd07:aaaa:bbbb:cccc::11]:3300]. The reporter's branch build produced this value and successfully formed a three-MON quorum; the correction was subsequently backported and an interim operator image was published.
solution.inference_hint: The accepted diagnosis is that the require-msgr2 configuration path directly appended ':3300' to an unbracketed IPv6 literal. Ceph then interpreted the port digits as part of the IPv6 address, visible in the MON's '[...::11:3300]:3300' probe value. Mapping the raw generated configuration and source comparison to this parsing failure is engineer-side inference.

edges.comment: Thread c27-c32: the reporter verified the correction on their own IPv6 cluster before the change was backported. The later interim-image publication is release logistics and is recorded only as context, not as a scored identifier or an additional verification requirement.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: the monitor configuration path used when msgr2 is required appended port 3300 to an unbracketed IPv6 literal, producing a malformed v2 endpoint that prevented the first MON from completing bootstrap.

Must ground the diagnosis in the collected evidence: bootstrap proceeds with the setting disabled, the failed configuration lacks inner IPv6 brackets, MON status shows the mangled address with the port effectively duplicated, and the adjacent working path produces a bracketed host and port.
Must fix endpoint generation with IPv6-safe host/port joining or equivalent correct bracketing, rather than treating requireMsgr2: false as the final resolution.

Must not treat the CSI ConfigMap workaround as the fix for initial MON bootstrap; that was a separate endpoint-parsing issue and maintainers explicitly said it would not resolve this bootstrap problem.
Must rely on affected-user verification before declaring resolution: a build containing the correction must generate the bracketed v2 endpoint and bring all three MONs into quorum.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced Kubernetes and Ceph operator who can inspect admin sockets and generated configuration, trace Go source, propose a patch, and build an operator image, but initially needs guidance for publishing and deploying a custom container image.
persona_hint.communication_style: Detailed, investigative, and cooperative; shares exact commands and raw outputs, tests hypotheses promptly, asks precise follow-up questions, and distinguishes MON bootstrap behavior from later MGR and OSD availability.
